title: PUB4 activates chitin signaling by ubiquitination-linked degradation of the immune suppressor FERONIA
content:
Abstract
Ubiquitination regulates pattern-triggered immune responses in plants, but the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. In Arabidopsis, the E3 ubiquitin ligase plant U-box protein 4 (PUB4) has been implicated in growth, development, and stress responses, and is known to interact with and be phosphorylated by chitin elicitor receptor kinase 1 (CERK1), resulting in the positive regulation of chitin-triggered immunity. In this study, we identified ubiquitinated proteins enriched from chitin-treated microsomal fractions and discovered that the receptor kinase FERONIA (FER) as a potential target of PUB4. FER interacted with PUB4 both in vivo and in vitro, as evidenced by yeast two-hybrid, bimolecular fluorescence complementation, and co-immunoprecipitation assays. An in vitro ubiquitination assay demonstrated that PUB4 ubiquitinates the cytoplasmic domain of FER. Moreover, transient expression assays in wild-type and pub4-2 mutant protoplasts revealed that PUB4 mediates chitin-induced FER degradation. Unlike PUB4, which positively regulates chitin-induced defense responses, FER negatively regulates them. For example, fer4 mutants exhibited elevated basal and chitin-induced reactive oxygen species and callose levels. This suggests that FER suppresses immune signaling under steady-state conditions, and that PUB4-mediated degradation of FER relieves this inhibition. These findings clearly reveal a novel mechanism by which PUB4 regulates chitin-induced immunity, driven by CERK1, through the targeted degradation of FER. This highlights the balance between positive and negative regulators of plant immune signaling.
